name: CCPA/CPRA
description: California Consumer Privacy Act (as amended by California Privacy Rights Act) overlay. Activated by personal information declarations. Covers consumer rights (access, deletion, correction, opt-out), business obligations (notice, purpose limitation, data minimization), service provider requirements, sensitive personal information handling, and automated decision-making disclosures.

evidence_requirements: Privacy policies implemented demonstrating compliance with CCPA/CPRA obligations (§1798.130(a)(5))
Policies updated at least every 12 months and posted at point of collection (§1798.130(a)(5))
Designated methods for consumers to submit requests documented (§1798.130(a))

When DC-MINOR applies: Affirmative opt-in consent from parent or guardian for consumers under 13 (CCPA §1798.120(c)); opt-in consent from consumer aged 13-15 before personal information sold or shared (§1798.120(c))
Privacy program accountability established — business responsible for CCPA/CPRA compliance (§1798.100)
Employee and contractor training on CCPA consumer rights handling (§1798.135(a)(3))
California Privacy Protection Agency (CPPA) cooperation procedures in place (§1798.199.40)
Risk assessments performed for processing that presents significant risk to consumer privacy (CPRA §1798.185(a)(15))
Risk assessments weigh benefits of processing against potential risks to consumer rights
Risk assessment documentation maintained and submitted to CPPA upon request

When DC-MINOR applies: Risk assessment documents heightened protection obligations — children's personal information subject to stricter opt-in requirements and prohibition on sale/sharing without affirmative authorization (§1798.120)
Consumer rights management process — right to know, delete, correct, opt-out, and limit SPI use (§§1798.100–1798.125)
Verifiable consumer requests responded to within 45 days, extendable by 45 days with notice (§1798.130(a)(2))
Non-discrimination policy — no retaliation against consumers exercising CCPA rights (§1798.125)

threshold_adjustments.reason: CCPA §§1798.100-1798.125 consumer rights — businesses must provide at least two methods for consumers to submit requests and respond within statutory timelines

evidence_requirements: Personal information inventory maintained — categories of PI collected, sold, shared, and disclosed for business purposes (§1798.110, §1798.115)
Sources of personal information documented for each category (§1798.110(c)(2))
Business or commercial purpose for each category of PI collection documented (§1798.110(c)(3))
Service provider and contractor agreements include CCPA-required terms — prohibit selling/sharing received PI (§1798.140(ag))
Contracts require service providers to notify business of inability to comply and grant right to remediate (§1798.140(ag)(1))
Sub-contractor flow-down — same CCPA obligations applied to downstream processors (§1798.140(ag)(2))
Data minimization principle applied — collection of PI reasonably necessary and proportionate to disclosed purposes (§1798.100(c))
Retention limited to what is reasonably necessary for disclosed purpose (§1798.100(d))
Storage limitation enforced — PI deleted or deidentified when no longer needed
Third-party inventory maintained — list of entities to which PI is sold or shared (§1798.115(c))
Categories of PI disclosed to each third party documented (§1798.115(c)(2))
Third-party due diligence — reasonable steps to ensure third parties use PI consistent with CCPA (§1798.100(d))
Data flow mapping — track PI disclosures for business purposes and sales/sharing to third parties (§1798.115)
Cross-context behavioral advertising transfers identified and disclosed (§1798.140(ah))
Consumer opt-out mechanisms for sale/sharing of PI across data flows (§1798.120)
Reasonable security procedures and practices appropriate to the nature of PI maintained (§1798.150)
Access controls implemented to protect PI from unauthorized access, destruction, use, modification, or disclosure (§1798.150(a))
Security measures commensurate with risk — failure constitutes grounds for private right of action for data breaches
Purpose limitation applied — PI used only for purposes disclosed at or before collection (§1798.100(a))
Secondary use prohibition — no further processing incompatible with disclosed purposes without additional notice (§1798.100(a))
Sensitive Personal Information use limited to purposes authorized by consumer or necessary for disclosed purpose (§1798.121)

When DC-MINOR applies: Permission scope configured to enforce prohibition on selling or sharing personal information of consumers under 16 without required opt-in consent; age verification mechanism in place or conservative assumption applied

threshold_adjustments.reason: CCPA §1798.100(a) purpose limitation — PI shall not be collected, used, retained, or disclosed in a manner inconsistent with reasonable consumer expectations

evidence_requirements: Privacy by design integrated into PI processing operations (§1798.100(c))
Data minimization at collection — only PI reasonably necessary for disclosed purpose (§1798.100(c))
Accuracy of PI maintained — reasonable steps to ensure correctness (§1798.106)
Encryption or redaction of PI as part of reasonable security measures (§1798.150 safe harbor)
Technical safeguards appropriate to the nature of the PI and the risks of the processing
Deidentification standards applied when PI no longer needed in identifiable form (§1798.140(m))
Records of consumer requests maintained for at least 24 months (§1798.130(a)(7) via regulations)
Processing records demonstrate compliance — categories of PI, purposes, and third-party disclosures documented (§1798.110, §1798.115)
Audit trail for consumer rights requests — request type, date received, response date, and outcome

threshold_adjustments.reason: CCPA §1798.130 recordkeeping and CPRA cybersecurity audit requirements — businesses must maintain verifiable records of consumer requests and compliance activities

evidence_requirements: Physical security measures protect PI from unauthorized access (§1798.150)
Physical access controls for systems and media containing PI
Hardware and media disposal procedures ensure PI is unrecoverable
Endpoint security measures protect PI on devices (§1798.150)
Remote access to PI secured with appropriate technical safeguards
Mobile and endpoint device management for systems processing PI
Right to delete process implemented — PI deleted within 45 days of verifiable request (§1798.105)
Deletion cascaded to service providers and contractors who received PI (§1798.105(c))
Deletion exceptions documented — legal obligations, security incidents, internal uses consistent with consumer expectations (§1798.105(d))
Breach detection capability — ability to identify unauthorized access to, or exfiltration of, PI (§1798.150)
Breach assessment process — determine whether breach involves unencrypted/unredacted PI triggering notification obligations
Security incident register maintained for all PI-related incidents
Ongoing monitoring of systems processing PI for security compliance (§1798.150)
Regular testing and evaluation of security procedures and practices
CPRA cybersecurity audit compliance — annual audit for businesses whose processing presents significant risk (§1798.185(a)(15))
Anomalous access detection — identify unusual access patterns to PI or bulk data exfiltration
Security monitoring appropriate to volume and sensitivity of PI processed
Automated decision-making technology monitoring — profiling activities reviewed for compliance (§1798.185(a)(16))
Cybersecurity audit performed annually for businesses whose processing presents significant risk (CPRA §1798.185(a)(15))
Security assessment program covers all systems processing PI
Vulnerability management — known vulnerabilities in PI processing systems remediated promptly
Breach notification to affected California residents in the most expedient time possible without unreasonable delay (Cal. Civ. Code §1798.82)
Notification includes nature of breach, categories of PI affected, and contact information for further inquiries
California Attorney General notified when breach affects more than 500 California residents (Cal. Civ. Code §1798.82(f))
Coordination with California Attorney General and CPPA during breach response as required
Remediation measures documented and implemented to address breach cause
Service provider and contractor breach notification procedures in place (§1798.140(ag))
Consumer notification in plain language describing the breach and affected PI categories (Cal. Civ. Code §1798.82(d))
Contact information provided for consumer credit reporting agencies when breach involves specified data elements
Identity theft prevention and mitigation information provided to affected consumers
Ability to restore availability and access to PI systems in timely manner following security incident
Business continuity procedures cover PI processing systems
Recovery procedures tested to validate PI can be restored without loss or corruption
Post-incident review to update security procedures and privacy risk assessments
Lessons learned documented and security measures updated to prevent recurrence
Recovery improvements incorporated into cybersecurity audit program

reporting_obligations.assessment_type: CPRA requires annual cybersecurity audits and risk assessments for businesses whose processing presents significant risk to consumer privacy (§1798.185(a)(15)). California AG may investigate and enforce. CPPA may audit.
reporting_obligations.reporting_entity: California Privacy Protection Agency (CPPA) for CCPA enforcement; California Attorney General for breaches affecting 500+ residents. Consumers may bring private right of action for data breaches under §1798.150.

notes: CCPA/CPRA applies to businesses with California consumers meeting revenue, data volume, or data-sale thresholds. This overlay adds CCPA/CPRA-specific adjustments and evidence fields on top of the AKSI v0.6 common-control catalog; controls without overlay-specific adjustments inherit the base AKSI definitions. CPRA amendments (effective Jan 2023) added data minimization (§1798.100(c)), purpose limitation (§1798.100(d)), cybersecurity audits (§1798.185(a)(15)), risk assessments, and automated decision-making disclosures. Breach notification follows California Civil Code §1798.82, which does not specify a fixed hour window but requires notification 'in the most expedient time possible.' Evidence retention set to 24 months per CCPA regulatory recordkeeping requirements.
